Left_EyeCenterX.blurb: Horizontal offset of the left eye (screen-left eye) in pixels from its nominal rest position. Positive moves it right on the LCD; negative left. Console range about −92…92 on Vector (half the 184 px face width).
Left_EyeCenterX.detail: Bound to s_faceDataOverride’s left-eye EyeCenterX via RegisterFaceWithConsoleVars. Only changes what you see when ProcFace_Display is Override individually or Override together, and only if this value differs from the baseline captured when override mode / ResetFace last baselined. In Normal mode the animation keyframe wins. “Left” means the eye on the left side of the screen, not Vector’s anatomical left. Under Override together, left-eye params (including this) are copied onto the right eye before draw.
Left_EyeCenterX.howTo: 1) Set ProcFace_Display to Override individually (or Override together). 2) Optionally call ResetFace so the baseline matches the current animation face. 3) Nudge this value and watch the left eye slide horizontally.

Left_EyeCenterY.blurb: Vertical offset of the left eye in pixels from its nominal rest height. Positive moves it down on the LCD; negative up. Console range about −48…48 on Vector (half the 96 px face height).
Left_EyeCenterY.detail: Same override-only path as Left_EyeCenterX: registered on s_faceDataOverride left-eye EyeCenterY, applied in Display Override modes when different from baseline. Combined with EyeCenterX, EyeScale, and EyeAngle into the per-eye warp matrix before the eye polygon is drawn.

Left_EyeScaleX.blurb: Horizontal scale of the left eye. 1.0 is nominal width (~43 px on Vector); larger makes that eye wider; 0 collapses it. Console range 0…10.
Left_EyeScaleX.detail: Override-face left EyeScaleX. Applied only under ProcFace_Display Override modes when changed from baseline. Independent of whole-face ProcFace_ScaleX. Multiplies NominalEyeWidth when building the eye polygon and transform.

Left_EyeScaleY.blurb: Vertical scale of the left eye. 1.0 is nominal height (~57 px on Vector); larger makes that eye taller; 0 flattens it. Console range 0…10.
Left_EyeScaleY.detail: Same override path as Left_EyeScaleX. LookAt and blink code also touch EyeScaleY on the live face; under override you freeze/sculpt via console instead of those systems for any param that differs from baseline.

Left_EyeAngle.blurb: Rotation of the left eye alone, in degrees, around that eye’s center. Positive and negative tilt the eye shape (and its lids/hotspot) like a cocked eyebrow. Console range −360…360.
Left_EyeAngle.detail: Maps to left-eye EyeAngle on the override ProceduralFace. Only visible under ProcFace_Display Override modes when different from baseline. Fed into GetTransformationMatrix with scale and center; does not rotate the whole face (use ProcFace_Angle_deg for that).

Left_LowerInnerRadiusX.blurb: How rounded the lower-inner corner of the left eye is, as a fraction of half-eye width (0 = sharp corner, 1 = fully rounded to the eye midline). Console range 0…1.
Left_LowerInnerRadiusX.detail: “Inner” means toward the nose / face center — for the screen-left eye that is the lower-right corner of that eye’s polygon. Multiplied by halfEyeWidth for ellipse2Poly. Override-only (with ProcFace_Display Override modes) when changed from baseline. Pair with Left_LowerInnerRadiusY for the vertical radius of the same corner.

Left_LowerInnerRadiusY.blurb: Vertical radius of the lower-inner (toward-nose) corner of the left eye, as a fraction of half-eye height. 0 = sharp; 1 = very round. Console range 0…1.
Left_LowerInnerRadiusY.detail: Paired with Left_LowerInnerRadiusX. Both must be > 0 for a curved corner; if either is 0 the drawer places a hard corner vertex instead of an ellipse arc.

Left_UpperInnerRadiusX.blurb: Horizontal rounding of the upper-inner (toward-nose) corner of the left eye, as a fraction of half-eye width. 0 = sharp; 1 = fully rounded. Console range 0…1.
Left_UpperInnerRadiusX.detail: For the screen-left eye this is the upper-right corner of that eye. Same override path as other radius params. Drawn with cv::ellipse2Poly using ProcFace_EllipseDelta as angular step.

Left_UpperInnerRadiusY.blurb: Vertical rounding of the upper-inner corner of the left eye, as a fraction of half-eye height. Console range 0…1.
Left_UpperInnerRadiusY.detail: Paired with Left_UpperInnerRadiusX. Both > 0 required for a curved arc; otherwise a hard corner.

Left_UpperOuterRadiusX.blurb: Horizontal rounding of the upper-outer corner of the left eye (away from the nose — left side of the left eye on screen), as a fraction of half-eye width. Console range 0…1.
Left_UpperOuterRadiusX.detail: “Outer” = toward the edge of the face. Same override + ellipse2Poly path as other corner radii. Useful for soft vs squared upper lids on the outer edge.

Left_UpperOuterRadiusY.blurb: Vertical rounding of the upper-outer corner of the left eye, as a fraction of half-eye height. Console range 0…1.
Left_UpperOuterRadiusY.detail: Paired with Left_UpperOuterRadiusX for the upper-left corner of the screen-left eye polygon.

Left_LowerOuterRadiusX.blurb: Horizontal rounding of the lower-outer corner of the left eye (outer/lower-left of that eye on screen), as a fraction of half-eye width. Console range 0…1.
Left_LowerOuterRadiusX.detail: Same override path as other radii. Outer = away from nose. Zero either X or Y radius of this corner → sharp vertex instead of arc.

Left_LowerOuterRadiusY.blurb: Vertical rounding of the lower-outer corner of the left eye, as a fraction of half-eye height. Console range 0…1.
Left_LowerOuterRadiusY.detail: Paired with Left_LowerOuterRadiusX for the lower-left corner of the screen-left eye.

Left_UpperLidY.blurb: How far the upper eyelid of the left eye closes. 0 = fully open (lid at top of eye); 1 = fully closed (lid reaches the bottom). Console range 0…1.
Left_UpperLidY.detail: Builds an upper-lid polygon that is filled black over the eye shape (negative space). Multiplied by NominalEyeHeight for pixel drop. Override-only under ProcFace_Display Override modes when changed from baseline. Combine with UpperLidAngle / UpperLidBend for squint, wink, or arched lids.

Left_UpperLidAngle.blurb: Tilts the left eye’s upper lid line in degrees. Positive/negative angles make one side of the lid drop more than the other (asymmetric squint). Console range −45…45.
Left_UpperLidAngle.detail: Used as tan(angle) to raise/lower the lid corners relative to each other, and as the rotation for the optional lid-bend ellipse. Override-only path with other Left_* sculpt params.

Left_UpperLidBend.blurb: Curves the left upper lid. 0 = straight lid edge; positive bends the lid down into the eye (soft droop); negative bends up away from the eye (arched). Console range −1…1.
Left_UpperLidBend.detail: Non-zero values add an ellipse2Poly arc to the upper-lid polygon. Negative bend uses fillPoly (concave) instead of fillConvexPoly. Scale is fraction of NominalEyeHeight. Override-only under ProcFace_Display Override modes.

Left_LowerLidY.blurb: How far the lower eyelid of the left eye closes. 0 = fully open (lid at bottom of eye); 1 = fully closed (lid reaches the top). Console range 0…1.
Left_LowerLidY.detail: Mirror of UpperLidY for the bottom lid: polygon filled black over the eye. Useful for tired looks, blinks, or lower squint. Override-only when ProcFace_Display is in an Override mode and the value differs from baseline.

Left_LowerLidAngle.blurb: Tilts the left eye’s lower lid line in degrees. Console range −45…45.
Left_LowerLidAngle.detail: Same geometry role as UpperLidAngle but for the lower-lid polygon and its bend arc. Override-only path.

Left_LowerLidBend.blurb: Curves the left lower lid. 0 = straight; positive bends up into the eye; negative bends down away from the eye. Console range −1…1.
Left_LowerLidBend.detail: Non-zero adds an ellipse arc to the lower-lid poly; negative bend uses non-convex fillPoly. Fraction of NominalEyeHeight. Override-only under ProcFace_Display Override modes.

Left_Lightness.blurb: Brightness multiplier for the filled left-eye pixels only. 1 = full strength; 0 blacks out that eye; values between dim it. Console range −1…1 (product faces use about 0…1; −1 is an animation “unset” sentinel).
Left_Lightness.detail: Applied in DrawEye after the global ProcFace_EyeLightnessMultiplier: each lit eye pixel is multiplied by this value. Only affects the display when ProcFace_Display is Override individually/together and this differs from the override baseline. Does not change hue (use ProcFace_Hue) or the CRT scanline path. Extreme negatives clamp toward black after cast.

Left_HotSpotCenterX.blurb: Horizontal position of the soft bright “hotspot” (pupil-like glow) inside the left eye, as a fraction of eye width. 0 = eye center; −1 = left edge; +1 = right edge. Console range −1…1.
Left_HotSpotCenterX.detail: Only visible when ProcFace_HotspotRender is on (otherwise eyes are flat fill). The hotspot center is warped with the same eye transform as the polygon, so it moves/rotates with Left_EyeAngle and scale. Override-only for the sculpt value itself under ProcFace_Display Override modes. Falloff width is global ProcFace_HotspotFalloff.
Left_HotSpotCenterX.howTo: 1) Enable ProcFace_HotspotRender. 2) Set ProcFace_Display to Override individually (or together). 3) Move this X (and Left_HotSpotCenterY) to place the bright core.

Left_HotSpotCenterY.blurb: Vertical position of the left eye’s soft hotspot, as a fraction of eye height. 0 = center; −1 = top edge; +1 = bottom edge. Console range −1…1.
Left_HotSpotCenterY.detail: Paired with Left_HotSpotCenterX. Same requires: ProcFace_HotspotRender for the glow to paint, and ProcFace_Display Override modes for this console value to replace the animation’s hotspot when it differs from baseline.
